posts.title: Building software that feels calm
posts.excerpt: A few practical principles for making complex products feel clear and capable.
posts.content:
Good software does not need to announce its complexity. The most useful systems give people a clear next step, make their state visible, and recover gracefully when something goes wrong.

For me, calmness starts with restraint. Every control should earn its place, every status message should reduce uncertainty, and every path should leave room for people to change their minds.

This is not minimalism for its own sake. It is respect for attention.

posts.title: Release notes are part of the product
posts.excerpt: Why a small, honest changelog can build more trust than a glossy launch page.
posts.content:
Release notes are a promise to the people who choose to use your work. They make progress legible and give users confidence that a product is alive.

The best notes are short, specific, and human. Say what changed, why it matters, and what you are still learning.
